name: How do Denver-area climate and home shifts affect backsplash installation?

mainEntity.name: How do Denver-area climate and home shifts affect backsplash installation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners throughout Aurora, Denver, and surrounding communities often face dry indoor air and foundation shifting caused by local expansive bentonite clay soils. These minor structural shifts can cause hairline movement where countertops meet drywall. In this climate, applying flexible, color-matched 100% silicone caulk along the bottom transition where the tile meets the countertop—rather than rigid grout—is essential. Silicone absorbs small movements and prevents cracking, whereas hard grout along that bottom seam tends to break away over time.
acceptedAnswer.description: Local soil movement and dry conditions require flexible silicone caulk where the backsplash meets the countertop, preventing cracked joints caused by minor seasonal settling.
